pr_title: Fix context menus not appearing when clicking outside of editor playfield's bounds
pr_body:
- Closes #18608 

`SelectionHandler` doesn't end up in the positional input queue while `BlueprintContainer` does due to the latter having a derived `ComposeBlueprintContainer` class that overrides the `ReceivePositionalInputAt` method to receive input outside its bounds.

Alternative solution would be defining a `ComposeSelectionHandler` that handles input everywhere as well, but I'm unsure if it's desired having another `ReceivePositionalInputAt` override rather than moving the context menu items to a better place.
pr_comments:
Honestly I think I'd prefer the `ComposeSelectionHandler` solution. The cross-class dependencies here feel a bit awkward, and having a `BlueprintContainer` display context menus which *only apply to selections* also sounds wrong.

That said, there's already pretty high coupling between these two classes so I'd be willing to let it slide for now and see where we end up. Definitely requires an inline comment explaining why the `ContextMenuItems` is done where it is, and mentioning the `ComposeBlueprintContainer`'s existence.

Interested in a second opinion on this. Make sure to have a look through `BlueprintContainer` as it may sway opinion (`BlueprintContainer` already uses `SelectionHandler`'s components a lot..).

I also don't really like this direction and would probably go the other proposed route, but simplify it even more by just adding the `ReceivePositionalInputAt` override to the base `SelectionHandler` itself rather than crafting inscrutable derived classes like `ComposeSelectionHandler` that don't really serve any discernible purpose. Would there be a problem with that approach?

Well, the selection handler used for compose screen specifically (main playfield one) is the one which should allow selecting out of bounds, while timeline should conform to its bounds. Having the context menu items moved one parent above means we don't have to copy the override from one place to another IMO, but I'm fine with going on the other direction and call it a day.

> the selection handler used for compose screen specifically (main playfield one) is the one which should allow selecting out of bounds

Why, though? In general a selection handler should be able to show a context menu for its selected items if the selection is visible. I'm not sure why the location matters, other than the fact that the bug being closed by this pull is in that one particular place.

If you can show a counterexample as to why that doesn't work then I may yield, but I'm looking to cut down on baroque inheritance hierarchies where possible.

Hmm, I think any sort of selection handler may be fine selecting outside its bounds as long as its own objects (my mind was thinking about conflicting with objects from another selection handler, but that should never be possible). 

That said, if we were to allow `SelectionHandler` to receive input outside bounds, then `BlueprintContainer` must surely do the same, since if the latter doesn't receive input there, the former wouldn't regardless of the overrides it has (right now it works because the blueprint container is a `ComposeBlueprintContainer` and that receives input outside bounds).

I believe it should be fine moving the `ReceivePositionalInputAt` override from `ComposeBlueprintContainer` to `BlueprintContainer`, will push that change for further testing here.

comments:
This is going to be caused by the whole hierarchy above the slider blueprint constricting input to the playfield, which doesn't sit well with `ContextMenuContainer`'s target location method:

![osu Game Tests 2022-06-08 at 06 20 48](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/172545862-7c82cace-5b62-429a-829d-93e8fe50264c.png)

Not sure if there's a simple solution here, may require some reconsideration of how `ContextMenuContainer` works.

`ContextMenuContainer` still sees the `HitObjectSelectionBlueprint` and all its parents (notably `BlueprintContainer`) despite being out of bounds, so we can still move context menu items one parent up from `SelectionHandler` to `BlueprintContainer` and have it handle outside-of-bound clicks.

review_comments:
I... don't really follow why this was removed? I'd say that removing this looks straight-up wrong. There's no reason the timeline blueprint container should receive input from all over, is there?

All I was asking for is for *selections* to be able to receive input even if partially obscured by its parents' bounds, not for some nebulous unification of behaviour between blueprint containers and selection handlers that doesn't even read correctly.

I don't follow, having `SelectionHandler` alone receiving input beyond bounds still requires `BlueprintContainer` to do the same as well, otherwise it's pointless. 

And regardless of whether `BlueprintContainer` receives input beyond bounds or not, it'll still be limited to its parent's bounds, unless it's parent also override `ReceivePositionalInputAt`, so there's not a single issue caused by making `TimelineBlueprintContainer` handle input outside bounds, as far as I'm understanding this.

I've also made it clear in the `BlueprintContainer` and `SelectionHandler` xmldoc that the point of receiving input outside bounds is only ever for interacting with blueprints that are partially (or fully, in case of timeline) outside bounds.

If `ReceivePositionalInputAt` works hierarchically as you describe (I don't recall, haven't gone and checked), then the issue I'm having is as follows: knowing that selection handlers are children of blueprint containers, it makes perfect sense to me that the selection handler should receive all inputs that its parenting blueprint container does. But should all composers receive all the positional inputs their parents do? I'm leaning no on that one.

I don't like the change, is all, especially given that - as you said - it essentially changes nothing at best. That said I'm abstaining from judgement on this one - I'm not going to merge it, but I'm also not going to block it.

`ReceivePositionalInputAt` does actually not affect whether children receive input outside bounds or not [as long as the parent is not masked](https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/blob/999f5c651c86dce41c8fbe85b2d879ec7a094cca/osu.Framework/Graphics/Containers/CompositeDrawable.cs#L1415), my bad on that part.

> knowing that selection handlers are children of blueprint containers, it makes perfect sense to me that the selection handler should receive all inputs that its parenting blueprint container does. But should all composers receive all the positional inputs their parents do? I'm leaning no on that one

Assuming by "composers" you mean `BlueprintContainer`s. Put it another way, without blueprint containers receiving input beyond their bounds, blueprints will not be selectable from there, while both composer and timeline allow it (would also imagine skin editor doing the same, if the blueprint container gets shrunk from the editor content). 

I believe this is an argument about whether all `BlueprintContainer`s should allow receiving input outside bounds, or each `BlueprintContainer` should manually specify that with a reference drawable (such as `Timeline` for timeline blueprint container). I don't really have a strong opinion on this either, will wait for others.
I'm not sure how I feel about this, but I'm happy to go with the current solution and revisit the next time we run into issues as a result of how it's implemented.
